UserAccount.title: UserAccount
UserAccount.description: Represents a primary user account, linked directly to an external authentication system (e.g., Firebase Authentication). This entity stores core user details but no sensitive authentication credentials.

id.description: Unique identifier for the UserAccount entity. This typically corresponds to the Firebase Authentication User ID (UID).

email.description: The email address associated with the user account, used for identification.

createdAt.description: Timestamp indicating when the user account was created.

lastLoginAt.description: Timestamp indicating the last time the user logged into the application.

UserProfile.title: UserProfile
UserProfile.description: Represents a distinct viewing profile associated with a UserAccount, allowing for personalized experiences (e.g., different watchlists, continue watching) under one main user. A single UserAccount can have multiple UserProfiles.

id.description: Unique identifier for the UserProfile entity.

userAccountId.description: Reference to the parent UserAccount this profile belongs to. (Relationship: UserAccount 1:N UserProfile)

name.description: The display name for the user profile (e.g., 'Kids Profile', 'John's Profile').

avatarUrl.description: URL to the avatar image chosen for this profile.

isKidProfile.description: Boolean flag indicating if this profile is designated as a 'kids' profile, potentially enabling content restrictions.

createdAt.description: Timestamp indicating when the user profile was created.

Genre.title: Genre
Genre.description: Defines a content genre, used for categorizing movies and shows (e.g., Action, Sci-Fi, Comedy).

id.description: Unique identifier for the Genre entity.

name.description: The name of the genre (e.g., 'Action', 'Science Fiction', 'Comedy').

description.description: An optional brief description of the genre.

Category.title: Category
Category.description: Defines a curated collection or dynamic grouping of content, such as 'Trending', 'Top Picks', or 'New Releases'. Distinct from genres, these are often for discovery and promotion.

id.description: Unique identifier for the Category entity.

name.description: The name of the category (e.g., 'Trending Now', 'Top Picks', 'Critically Acclaimed').

description.description: A description explaining the purpose or content of the category.

displayOrder.description: An optional numeric value to determine the display order of categories in the UI.

Movie.title: Movie
Movie.description: Represents a single piece of streamable content, such as a movie or a TV show episode, with all its associated metadata.

id.description: Unique identifier for the Movie entity.

title.description: The main title of the movie or show.

description.description: A brief synopsis or tagline for the content.

thumbnailUrl.description: URL to the primary thumbnail or poster image for the movie, typically hosted in Firebase Storage.

videoUrl.description: URL to the main video file for the movie, typically hosted in Firebase Storage.

trailerUrl.description: URL to a short trailer or preview video, typically hosted in Firebase Storage.

durationMinutes.description: The total duration of the movie or episode in minutes.

releaseYear.description: The year the content was originally released.

ageRating.description: The official age rating of the content (e.g., 'G', 'PG', 'PG-13', 'R', 'NC-17', 'TV-MA').

userRating.description: An average user rating for the movie, typically on a scale of 0 to 5 or 0 to 10.

genreIds.description: An array of IDs referencing the genres this movie belongs to. (Relationship: Genre N:N Movie)

categoryIds.description: An array of IDs referencing the categories this movie belongs to (e.g., 'Trending', 'Top Picks'). (Relationship: Category N:N Movie)

createdAt.description: Timestamp indicating when the movie metadata was first added to the system.

updatedAt.description: Timestamp indicating the last time the movie metadata was updated.

WatchlistItem.title: WatchlistItem
WatchlistItem.description: Represents a specific movie or show that a UserProfile has added to their personalized 'My List' or watchlist.

id.description: Unique identifier for the WatchlistItem entity.

userProfileId.description: Reference to the UserProfile that added this item to their watchlist. (Relationship: UserProfile 1:N WatchlistItem)

movieId.description: Reference to the Movie that is on the watchlist. (Relationship: Movie 1:N WatchlistItem)

addedAt.description: Timestamp indicating when the movie was added to the watchlist.

ContinueWatchingItem.title: ContinueWatchingItem
ContinueWatchingItem.description: Stores the playback state for a movie or show, allowing a UserProfile to resume watching from where they left off.

id.description: Unique identifier for the ContinueWatchingItem entity.

userProfileId.description: Reference to the UserProfile that is watching this content. (Relationship: UserProfile 1:N ContinueWatchingItem)

movieId.description: Reference to the Movie being watched. (Relationship: Movie 1:N ContinueWatchingItem)

playbackPositionSeconds.description: The timestamp in seconds from the beginning of the video where the user last stopped watching.

lastWatchedAt.description: Timestamp indicating the last time this content was actively watched by the user profile.

isCompleted.description: Boolean flag indicating whether the user has watched the entire movie/episode.

firestore.reasoning:
The Firestore structure for 'Replica' is designed to be secure, scalable, and highly debuggable by strictly adhering to the core design principles and strategy mandates. 

**Authorization Independence (CRITICAL) & Denormalization:**
To eliminate the need for `get()` calls in Firestore Security Rules, which are costly and complex, authorization context is denormalized directly into the child documents. For instance:
1.  **UserAccount:** The `userAccountId` (which corresponds to `request.auth.uid`) is the document ID for `/userAccounts/{userAccountId}`. This makes authentication a direct path match (`request.auth.uid == userAccountId`).
2.  **UserProfile:** Resides at `/userAccounts/{userAccountId}/userProfiles/{userProfileId}`. The `UserProfile` document itself includes `userAccountId` as a field. This allows rules to check `request.auth.uid == resource.data.userAccountId` without fetching the parent `UserAccount` document.
3.  **WatchlistItem & ContinueWatchingItem:** These are subcollections of `UserProfile`. Each `WatchlistItem` and `ContinueWatchingItem` document explicitly includes both `userAccountId` and `userProfileId` as fields. This denormalization allows rules to verify ownership like `request.auth.uid == resource.data.userAccountId && request.resource.data.userProfileId == userProfileId` directly from the document's own data, completely avoiding `get()` calls on `UserProfile` or `UserAccount` documents. This is vital for atomic write operations and overall rule efficiency.

**QAPs (Query as Authorization Predicate) & Structural Segregation:**

The structure ensures that `list` operations are secure and performant:
1.  **User-Specific Data (`/userAccounts/{userAccountId}/...`):** User profiles, watchlists, and continue watching items are organized hierarchically under a user's unique ID (`/userAccounts/{userAccountId}`). Security rules will enforce that a user can only access documents within their own `userAccountId` path. For example, a rule `match /userAccounts/{userAccountId}/userProfiles/{userProfileId} { allow read, write: if request.auth.uid == userAccountId; }` means any `list` query for `userProfiles` will inherently only return data for the authenticated user, as querying across different `userAccountId` paths would be denied. This fulfills the QAP by making the authorization predicate part of the query path.
2.  **Global/Public Data (`/genres`, `/categories`, `/movies`):** These collections hold content metadata that is universally readable by all authenticated users. Their security posture is homogenous (read-all for users, write-only for admins). Since all documents within these collections share the same access rules, `list` queries are inherently secure without needing complex server-side filtering. Admin access is controlled via the `/roles_admin/{adminUid}` collection, where the mere existence of a document for a `uid` grants administrative privileges, allowing rules like `allow create, update, delete: if exists(/databases/$(database)/documents/roles_admin/$(request.auth.uid));`. This separation of concerns simplifies rules and supports QAPs for both public and private data models.
